title: After jokes on GBH, state senator says agritourism like corn mazes are serious business
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Massachusetts Senator Jo Comerford defends agritourism, proposing $5 million to promote activities like corn mazes amid farmer struggles.
Comerford criticizes GBH radio hosts for mocking agritourism, inviting them to western Massachusetts to understand its economic significance.
Agritourism amendment passed with other 'fun agenda' items; Massachusetts farmers face financial difficulties, losing 5.5% of farmland recently.

title: Red Sox trade Marcelo Mayer to Giants for reliever Erik Miller
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Red Sox traded shortstop Marcelo Mayer to the Giants for reliever Erik Miller and minor leaguer Carlos Gutierrez.
Mayer, a former top prospect, faced durability and offensive challenges, playing 114 games with a .223 average for Boston.
Miller, 28, brings a 2.76 ERA and 45 strikeouts to Boston's bullpen, enhancing their late-inning pitching options.

title: Patriots sign former Giants defensive tackle Casey Rogers
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Patriots signed 27-year-old defensive tackle Casey Rogers, who previously played on the Giants and Bills' practice squads.
Rogers played 10 games with the DC Defenders in the United Football League, recording 21 tackles and 1.5 sacks.
He joins a strong Patriots defensive line led by Milton Williams and Christian Barmore, participating in practice in Foxborough.

title: 5 things to know about new Red Sox catcher Adley Rutschman
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Boston Red Sox acquired Adley Rutschman from Baltimore Orioles as part of a trade involving multiple players and prospects.
Rutschman is a former No. 1 MLB draft pick with a history of strong offensive and defensive contributions.
Injuries have limited Rutschman to 67 games this season, impacting his offensive performance compared to earlier years.

title: 5 takeaways from Day 8 of Patriots training camp
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: A.J. Brown played through a dislocated thumb, making key plays in the red-zone drills against Christian Gonzalez.
Efton Chism impressed with multiple touchdowns during scrimmage, while Mack Hollins and Kayshon Boutte spent time with the second team.
Undrafted cornerback Channing Canada stood out with crucial pass breakups and participated in kickoff return practice.

title: Ballot Brief: Your guide to the 2026 midterms
author: Zipporah Osei
bullets: Massachusetts 2026 midterms include governor's race, U.S. Senate, congressional contests, and nine statewide ballot questions.
Early voting for the Massachusetts midterms starts on August 22, with primaries scheduled for September 1.
Boston.com's Ballot Brief newsletter offers updates on candidate debates, statewide issues, and important voting information.

title: Somerville man accused of World Cup ticket scam that netted $14K
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Robert Whelan of Somerville is accused of a $14,000 World Cup ticket scam involving fake tickets.
Whelan allegedly used his Patriots season ticket holder status to claim priority access to World Cup tickets.
He created false email confirmations and was arraigned with bail set at $250; next court date is Sept. 23.

title: Man charged with kidnapping, raping door-to-door salesperson in Everett
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: James Mugford, 67, charged with kidnapping and raping a door-to-door salesperson in Everett.
The victim was allegedly assaulted while selling phone plans at Mugford's Fremont Avenue home.
Mugford held without bail; arraigned on charges including aggravated rape and kidnapping.

title: Red Sox acquire catcher Adley Rutschman from Orioles
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Red Sox acquire catcher Adley Rutschman from the Orioles in exchange for Carlos Narvaez and multiple prospects.
Rutschman, a three-time All-Star, enhances Boston's catching corps with strong defense and offensive potential.
Rutschman is expected back soon from injury and is under Red Sox control through the 2027 season.

title: The top four fall foliage destinations in the U.S. are not in New England, according to Priceline
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: Priceline ranked the top four fall foliage destinations outside New England as Adirondacks, Columbia River Gorge, Aspen, and Bucks County.
Bretton Woods, NH, Berkshires, MA, and Stowe, VT secured the No. 5, 8, and 9 spots in Priceline's 2026 list.
Priceline's ranking is based on hotel searches by U.S.-based consumers for October dates in areas known for fall foliage.
